name: death-and-high-scores
demonstrates: CYBERPUN-17-13's death-screen/high-scores/RUN AGAIN surface, driven end-to-end from a running game rather than screenshotted at a guessed timestamp. GameScene.advanceMovementAndCamera transitions to .death once per .gameplay frame when player.hp <= 0 (PlayerDeathTriggerTests), after which DeathScreenNode records the run into HighScoreStore exactly once and renders the real eight-row summary from the live runStats/playerCombat/runElapsedSeconds. Rather than waiting a fixed guessed duration for HP to reach zero, this journey wait_for_elements on the RUN AGAIN button itself, which only mounts once .death is entered -- so the capture is taken exactly when the death screen is actually up, regardless of exactly how many bites (BiteComponent.biteDamage=5 against PlayerNode.baseMaxHP=100, i.e. ~20 contact bites once the swarm reaches the standoff ring) it took to get there. WAIT_FOR_ELEMENT IS BACKSTOPPED BY A DERIVED FLOOR WAIT, NOT TRUSTED ALONE: this is the first journey in the tree to use that verb (menu-to-gameplay, raccoon-swarm, pickup-spawn and auto-fire-weapons all reach their frames with explicit waits), and the probe's default element timeout is not documented anywhere in this repo -- so if that default were shorter than the run, the step would fall through and death-screen-summary would capture a gameplay frame labelled as the death screen, the same 'empty rooftop reads as feature missing' failure JourneyManifestTests exists for. Each wait_for_element is therefore preceded by an explicit 32s wait, which sits just above the floor JourneyManifestTests.secondsBeforeThePlayerCanBeDead derives from the production constants (~30.7s: RaccoonSpawnDirector.initialSpawnInterval 3s, plus the guaranteed ~1,056pt off-screen spawn gap walked in at RaccoonSeekBehavior.pointsPerSecond, plus the 19 further BiteComponent.biteIntervalSeconds needed for 20 bites of biteDamage 5 to drain PlayerNode.baseMaxHP 100) -- so wait_for_element only ever has to cover the tail of the run rather than all ~31s of it. Overshoot is harmless in the other direction, because DeathScreenNode mounts no auto-dismiss and the death screen stays up until a button is tapped; the failure mode is one-sided, which is what makes this belt and braces rather than a second guess. JourneyManifestTests.test_theDeathJourneysWaitForElementSteps_areBackstoppedByADerivedFloorWait binds both waits to that derived floor, so a CI-speedup trim of the literals, or a retune of the spawn/seek/bite constants that moves the floor, fails in-suite instead of silently mislabelling a capture. WHAT death-screen-summary IS REVIEWED FOR (AC1): the eight rows -- SURVIVED, RACCOONS DOWN, LEVEL, RABIES, DAMAGE DEALT, KILL BONUS, SURVIVAL, SCORE -- all rendered with real, non-placeholder values from this run. The journey then taps RUN AGAIN once (AC5's end-to-end path: GameScene.startNewRun() draws a fresh worldSeed and transitions straight back to .gameplay with no menu detour) and confirms the app is still alive and back in a playable scene -- the new-seed/new-junction VALUE itself is not something a screenshot can distinguish from the old one, so that half stays pinned by GameStateMachineTests/RunSpawnSelectorTests, not by this probe. The second death IS chained off that RUN AGAIN run: there is no menu detour and no second PLAY in between -- the fresh run started by RUN AGAIN is driven straight to a second .death, this time exiting via BACK TO MENU (also pinned live: DeathScreenNode's BACK TO MENU handler and GameStateMachine's death -> menu transition) so the probe can reach .menu and then .highScores. WHAT high-scores-table IS REVIEWED FOR: the runs just played appearing as real rows -- rank, score and the run's own values -- in the top-10 table rendered by HighScoresScreenNode from a live HighScoreStore, rather than an empty 'NO RUNS YET' table or placeholder rows. THE FIRST OF TWO THINGS THIS PROBE CANNOT COVER, AND WHY NEITHER IS A REGRESSION: this frame does NOT evidence AC1's persistence half. The probe never relaunches the app, so the table it renders is read back from the same in-memory HighScoreStore instance the run was recorded into on the death screen, and no screenshot of it can distinguish 'written to UserDefaults and read back after a cold start' from 'held in memory since DeathScreenNode.willEnter()'. Persistence across a relaunch stays owned by HighScoreStoreTests.test_recordRun_persistsAcrossSimulatedRelaunch, which records into one HighScoreStore and then reads the table back through a SECOND store over the same UserDefaults suite -- the same 'named in the brief as a probe limitation, pinned in-suite instead' treatment AC7 gets below, and a reviewer must not sign persistence off from this frame. THE SECOND THING THIS PROBE CANNOT COVER: AC7 (portrait/landscape layout, RUN AGAIN/BACK TO MENU never overlapping) has no corresponding step here because the probe's supported step vocabulary (wait / screenshot / assert_running / navigate / tap_at / wait_for_element, enforced by JourneyManifestTests.supportedActions) has no rotate/orientation verb -- the same documented limitation pattern as auto-fire-weapons.json's 'no bullet frame, by design' note. AC7 stays owned by ScreensTests's orientation overlap suite, which already pins it against real button frames in both orientations; its absence from these screenshots must be read as this probe-vocabulary limitation, not as the acceptance criterion being unmet. Gate is human/vision review of the two screenshots; assert_running steps only confirm the app process is still alive.
